display.purpose: The oversized two-line name in the hero.

body.purpose: Navigation, summaries, descriptions, and article links.

components.name: Engineering Hero

components.html:
FabioRosado

Senior Software Engineer

I build backend systems and developer tools for reliable software.
components.css: .ds-hero-heading { margin: 0; } .ds-hero-name-first, .ds-hero-name-second { display: block; overflow: visible; color: var(--paper); font: 400 clamp(54px, 8.92vw, 137px)/0.78 'DM Serif Display', Georgia, serif; letter-spacing: -0.04em; white-space: nowrap; } .ds-hero-name-second { color: var(--coral); font-size: clamp(60px, 9.7vw, 149px); } .ds-hero-role { color: var(--paper); font: 700 clamp(21px, 2.15vw, 33px)/1.2 Manrope, sans-serif; letter-spacing: -0.025em; } .ds-hero-summary { color: var(--muted); font: 400 clamp(14px, 1.25vw, 19px)/1.45 Manrope, sans-serif; } @media (max-width: 1050px) { .ds-hero-name-first, .ds-hero-name-second { font-size: clamp(66px, 17vw, 110px); line-height: 0.82; } .ds-hero-role { max-width: 100%; font-size: clamp(27px, 7vw, 42px); white-space: normal; } .ds-hero-summary { max-width: 34ch; font-size: 14px; line-height: 1.55; } } @media (max-width: 420px) { .ds-hero-name-first, .ds-hero-name-second { font-size: clamp(60px, 17vw, 74px); } .ds-hero-role { font-size: clamp(21px, 6.2vw, 26px); } .ds-hero-summary { max-width: 30ch; } }

components.name: Conceptual Architecture Illustration
components.description: One unframed architecture illustration: layered plum planes around a coral core, green routes connected at ports, and a subordinate schematic console plane. It contains no text, code, or metrics and makes no production-system claim. The preview embeds the smallest WebP derived from src/assets/hero-architecture.png.
components.css: .ds-hero-illustration { display: flex; margin: 0; align-items: center; justify-content: center; } .ds-hero-architecture { display: block; width: 100%; height: 100%; object-fit: contain; } @media (max-width: 1050px) { .ds-hero-illustration { width: 100%; max-width: 680px; margin-top: 8px; align-self: center; } .ds-hero-architecture { height: auto; max-height: 360px; } }

narrative.overview:
The homepage presents Fabio as a Senior Software Engineer. A strong DM Serif Display treatment gives his name a distinct identity; concise Manrope copy explains his work; and one conceptual architecture illustration gives the hero depth and technical character. Deep plum, coral, and electric green retain their established roles.

The desktop composition pairs the hero with the architecture illustration, then places full external project cards beside recent writing. About copy and social links complete the page. At mobile widths, content becomes a single vertical sequence and the full illustration sits beneath the hero copy.
keyCharacteristics: Deep plum, coral, and electric green palette
One cohesive architecture illustration with layered components, connected routes, and a coral focal point
Factual project descriptions with concise focus and technology labels

rules.name: The Green Annotation Rule
rules.body: Use green for concise labels, illustrated signal routes, outlines, focus indicators, and hover feedback; keep larger fields plum or coral.

rules.name: The Serif Identity Rule
rules.body: Reserve DM Serif Display for Fabio's name. Use Manrope for the role, project titles, navigation, and explanatory copy; use monospace for concise technical labels.

rules.name: The Conceptual Architecture Rule
rules.body: Pair the hero copy with one cohesive, unframed architecture illustration. Preserve its layered plum components, coral core, and meaningful green connections; show the full silhouette as it stacks below the copy. It contains no fabricated code, metrics, or production claims.

rules.name: The Full Project Link Rule
rules.body: Make each project card one complete external link with factual copy and concise focus or technology labels; leave cards free of decorative abstract art.

rules.name: The Flat Surface Rule
rules.body: Use tonal gradients and fine borders without CSS drop shadows on interface surfaces; project cards stay square-cornered. The architecture illustration carries its own layered depth and internal shading.

rules.name: The Accessible Motion Rule
rules.body: Keep visible green focus-visible outlines and honor reduced-motion preferences.

dos: Do keep the confirmed plum, coral, and green palette in their established roles.
Do preserve strong serif identity typography and use sans-serif project titles.
Do keep the hero illustration cohesive, with layered plum components, meaningful green connections, and a coral focal point.
Do keep project descriptions factual and project focus or technology labels concise.
Do make each entire project card an external link.
Do retain clear focus-visible feedback and honor reduced-motion preferences.
donts: Don't add decorative abstract art to project cards.
Don't use electric green as a large background field.
Don't add CSS drop shadows to interface surfaces or round project cards.
